Orff Studio sample audio
========================

Source: GeneralUser GS 1.471
Author: S. Christian Collins
Copyright: 1997-2015 by S. Christian Collins
Official source: https://schristiancollins.com/generaluser.php

These MP3 files were rendered from the user's supplied SoundFont using TinySoundFont. No source SF2 is distributed with this website. The exact embedded SoundFont license follows:

***     License v2.0    ***

** License of the complete work **
You may use GeneralUser GS without restriction for your own music creation, private or commercial.  This SoundFont bank is provided to the community free of charge.  Please feel free to use it in your software projects, and to modify the SoundFont bank or its packaging to suit your needs.

** License of contained samples **
GeneralUser GS inherits the usage rights of the samples contained within, all of which allow full use in music production, including the ability to make profit from musical recordings created with GeneralUser GS.

Many of the samples are original, but some were taken from other banks freely (and legally) available on the Internet from various SoundFont websites.  Because GeneralUser GS originated as a personal project with no intention for publication, I cannot be 100% sure where all of the samples originated, although I do know that none of them came from commercially published SoundFont packages or sample CDs.  Regardless, many "free" SoundFonts available on the web may indeed contain samples of questionable origin.  My understanding of the copyrights of all samples is only as good as the information provided by the original sources. If you become aware of any restricted samples being used in GeneralUser GS, please let me know so I can replace them.

This uncertainty may concern you if you intend to use GeneralUser GS in a commercial software product.  That being said, I have never received any complaint regarding sample ownership since I published the original GeneralUser GS back in 2000, and as far as I am aware, neither have any of the companies creating commercial software products using GeneralUser GS.

** More info **
If you plan to feature GeneralUser GS on your own website, please do not link directly to my download files.  Either link to my website, or provide your own local copy instead.

I hope you enjoy GeneralUser GS!  This SoundFont bank is the product of many years of hard work.

You can find updates to GeneralUser GS and more of my SoundFonts at:
http://www.schristiancollins.com

I can be reached at: s_chriscollins@hotmail.com.

Thank you!
-Chris

Renderer: TinySoundFont, https://github.com/schellingb/TinySoundFont
See TSF-LICENSE.txt in the reproducible build sources.

Instrument substitutions are described in manifest.json. These are General MIDI approximations where an exact Orff sample was unavailable; the website allows replacement samples.

Additional recorded percussion (CC0):
Finger Cymbals #1 — Joseph SARDIN / BigSoundBank.com
Gong1 mf — Versilian Studios LLC / Versilian Community Sample Library
See recorded/CREDITS.txt and recorded/CC0-1.0.txt for sources and processing.


RECORDER CONSORT: Separate acoustic soprano, alto, tenor and bass recorder recordings from the Versilian Community Sample Library (VCSL), Versilian Studios LLC, CC0-1.0. These replace the GeneralUser recorder approximation in Orff Atelier. Full source hashes, pinned source commit, pitch calibration and seamless-loop processing details: recorded/recorders/PROVENANCE.json and recorded/recorders/CREDITS.txt. Source and license: https://versilian-studios.com/vcsl/

ADDITIONAL ORFF ENSEMBLE VOICES
Contrabass bars: adapted soft-strike low VCSL marimba recordings, not a recording of an Orff contrabass model. Tambourine, shakers, sleigh bells and cabasa: recorded VCSL performances. Maracas: FreePats World and Rare Percussion recordings. All source recordings for these additions are CC0. Complete source URLs, authorship, mapping, transformations and hashes are preserved in recorded/ensemble-additions/CREDITS.txt and PROVENANCE.json.

TEMPLE BLOCKS
Five individual hard-mallet strikes from a five-piece composite temple-block set, by sazanami12 / Freesound, CC0-1.0. Source: https://freesound.org/people/sazanami12/sounds/863784/
The public HQ MP3 preview was used, not the original WAV. Native pitches retained; excerpts trimmed, level-balanced, gently high-passed and faded. Full source/derived hashes and processing: recorded/temple-blocks/PROVENANCE.json and CREDITS.txt.

WIND CHIMES / BAR CHIMES
Five Bar Chimes Samples by tosha73 / Freesound, CC0-1.0. Source: https://freesound.org/people/tosha73/sounds/495327/
Five acoustic sweeps extracted from the user-supplied original 44.1 kHz stereo WAV: down brisk/slow and up brisk/medium/slow. Native pitches, speeds and ringing tails retained; levels balanced. See recorded/wind-chimes/CREDITS.txt and PROVENANCE.json.

AGOGO BELLS, COWBELL AND SLAPSTICK
Acoustic low/high agogo bells, open/muted cowbell and slapstick clap from Versilian Studios LLC / VCSL, CC0-1.0. Native pitches and speeds retained. Source: https://versilian-studios.com/vcsl/
See recorded/bells-slapstick/CREDITS.txt and PROVENANCE.json for pinned source URLs, hashes and processing.

WOODBLOCK
The original GeneralUser woodblock mapping is replaced with two acoustic recordings: VCSL woodblock by Versilian Studios LLC (low), and Block "Meinl" in wood #0466 by Joseph SARDIN / BigSoundBank (high). Both CC0-1.0. Native pitches and wooden attacks retained; levels balanced.
Sources: https://versilian-studios.com/vcsl/ and https://bigsoundbank.com/block-meinl-in-wood-s0466.html
See recorded/woodblock/CREDITS.txt and PROVENANCE.json for source/derived hashes and processing.


Street Song instrument additions
================================

CASTANETS
Castanets (simple), sound #0922, by Joseph SARDIN / BigSoundBank.com.
Source: https://bigsoundbank.com/castanets-simple-s0922.html
Original WAV: https://bigsoundbank.com/UPLOAD/bwf-en/0922.wav
License: CC0 1.0 Universal (public domain dedication).
https://bigsoundbank.com/licenses.html
Two separate single strokes selected from the unclipped opening of the recording.
Native pitch; silence/tails trimmed, constant gain, endpoint fades, polyphase
48 kHz to 44.1 kHz resampling, TPDF dither to 16-bit PCM WAV.

SIDE DRUM
Rope-tension snare drum, high tension, snares on, velocity layer 3, round robins
1 and 3. Recorded by Versilian Studios LLC / Versilian Community Sample Library.
Source: https://github.com/sgossner/VCSL
Source commit: c1ea7bcc3c7309650ab0da9d15c9cd1fbc4a4c7e
License: CC0 1.0 Universal.
https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
Natural pitch and decay retained. Constant gain and endpoint fades only,
with TPDF dither to 44.1 kHz stereo 16-bit PCM WAV.

SOPRANINO RECORDER IN F — TRANSPOSED APPROXIMATION
Uses the existing CC0 VCSL Baroque Soprano Recorder recordings, raised five
semitones (a perfect fourth) to cover F5–F7. This is not a separate physical
sopranino recording. Existing buffer-relative sustain loops and fine pitch
corrections are retained. No source bytes are duplicated or changed.
See ../recorders/PROVENANCE.json and CREDITS.txt for the original source paths,
hashes, tuning and loop preparation. Existing native SATB recorders are unchanged.

TIMPANI
Uses the existing C2–C4 chromatic samples rendered from GeneralUser GS 1.471,
by S. Christian Collins, with TinySoundFont. No audio bytes are changed.
Source: https://schristiancollins.com/generaluser.php
License: GeneralUser GS License v2.0, reproduced in ../../CREDITS.txt.

PROVENANCE.json records source and output hashes, transformations and mapping.
manifest-fragment.json contains instrumentSamples entries for app integration.
